newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Parana state soy plantings to rise 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Parana state soy plantings to rise 11 pct.

text.p: Soybean plantings in Brazil's key Parana state in 1997/98 should reach 2.75 million hectares, up 10.66 percent from the 2.48 million hectares planted in 1996/97, the state agricultural secretariat said.
Production with normal weather conditions could reach 7.3 million tonnes, a rise of 11.72 percent on output of 6.53 million tonnes in 1996/97, the secretariat said in a statement.

Norberto Ortigara, director of the secretariat's rural economy department, said farmers were opting to plant soybeans because of last year's prices which averaged 15.60 reais a 60-kg bag against traditional prices of 12 to 13 reais a bag.
If confirmed, the planted area would be the largest ever, Ortigara said.
Independent consultants Safras e Mercado have also recently estimated farmers in the state would plant 2.76 million hectares with soybeans, with production forecast at 7.31 million tonnes.
